# Objective

Implement the bounded G9C constructive composed-spatial-object model on
`feature/g9c-composed-spatial-objects`.

**PROPOSED FUTURE PROMPT — UNEXECUTED AND NOT AUTHORIZED.**

# Mandatory entry gate

Require author-approved G9B PASS, approved G9C boundary and canonical models,
clean branch, prompt hash and green G8/G9A/G9B plus composed verification.

# Hard dependencies

Author-approved G9B primitive schemas on the G9A3 substrate are the hard
semantic dependency. U0/X1/U1, G9O1 and U2 are not prerequisites.

# Recommended execution predecessor

Execute directly after G9B on the spatial track. Parallel application/operations
work may already be complete, but cannot define composite topology.

# Global/release gate

G9C closes the productive spatial track and joins U1 at the global G9 closeout.
Its phase PASS is not the global author approval required by U2.

# Authority and evidence hierarchy

Read implemented G9A/B semantics and current kernel primitives first, then the
approved composed boundary, CeDG canonical models and validation contracts.

# Scope

Implement only approved spatial point collections/curves/arcs, edges, oriented
loops, faces, supporting/ruled/developable surfaces, incidence, adjacency,
orientation, boundary ownership and connected components needed by CeDG.

# Explicitly forbidden scope

No opaque CAD feature tree, generic solid modeller, boolean kernel, meshing as
truth, manufacturing topology, hidden projection correspondence, U2 procedures,
or broader surface families without approval.

# Editable boundaries

GeoCeDG shared spatial composite packages, minimum serialization/factory seams,
canonical models/tests, docs/evidence/verifier and registered upstream edits.

# Productive versus test-private permissions

Only approved constructive topology is productive. Research surfaces/solid
algorithms remain test-private and cannot establish public support.

# Architectural placement

Identity, incidence, adjacency, orientation and projection bindings belong to
the shared semantic model; rendering meshes and exporters are derived clients.

# Required design/specification

Implement explicit ownership, oriented boundary loops, closure/manifold
diagnostics where claimed, component projection coherence, revisions and atomic
invalidity according to the approved boundary. Component coherence uses the
declared ProjectionSystem and diagram maps only after intrinsic certificates;
screen layout never repairs topology or correspondence.

# Geometric invariants and degeneracies

Cover open/nonmanifold/inconsistently oriented boundaries, coincident edges,
degenerate faces, disconnected components, support loss and dynamic topology
change without stale results.

# Compatibility and serialization

Use G9A/B IDs/schema versions and explicit component references. Old files stay
unassociated; meshes never replace constructive serialized authority.

# Required tests and commands

Run tetrahedron, cylinder/cone definitions, composite oriented boundary,
developable/ruled cases, invalid topology, dynamic degeneration, roundtrip,
determinism and functional counters; focused G9C plus composed verification.

# Required artifacts

Source/tests/models, boundary/capability matrix, scientific evidence, benchmarks,
verifier, traceability and G9 closeout inputs.

# Stop conditions

Stop if CAD feature history becomes authority, projection coherence cannot be
certified, topology is inferred visually, or scope requires a generic B-Rep.
